title.value: On the Expressivity of Markov Reward
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document and reflects the main topic of the paper — the expressivity of Markov Reward functions.
title.quote: On the Expressivity of Markov Reward

analysis.description: This paper explores the expressivity of reward in reinforcement learning, particularly focusing on Markov Reward functions and their ability to encode various types of tasks. The paper introduces three new task notions and discusses limitations in expressivity through empirical and theoretical findings. It also offers algorithms for constructing reward functions that can optimize these tasks.

type.justification: The paper primarily discusses theoretical aspects of reward expressivity in reinforcement learning, supported by proofs, mathematical formulations, and theorems regarding the limitations and capabilities of Markov Reward functions within this theoretical framework.
type.quote: Our main results prove that while reward can express many of these tasks, there exist instances of each task type that no Markov reward function can capture.

name.justification: The paper discusses concepts such as reward functions, Markov Decision Processes, and reinforcement learning agents, all of which are central to the field of Reinforcement Learning.
name.quote: Reward is the driving force for reinforcement-learning agents.

name.justification: The broader exploration within reinforcement learning is part of the machine learning research area, especially since reinforcement learning itself is a subfield of machine learning.
name.quote: How are we to use algorithms for reinforcement learning (RL) to solve problems of relevance in the world?
